summary:
The plan is in plan.md. It gives each of the eight plots exact block coordinates. Every house uses the same layout: storeys at y1–2 and y4–5 with ground floors level with the street, a front gable, a hip or a lean-to roof, and front doors on the south (high z) as the brief says.
The variety reads as the Presidio: a white house with a steep red roof, a porch and a brick chimney; a cream Mission duplex with a curved front parapet and two doors; a white garage and shed with dark grey roofs; a brick barracks with a two-storey white colonnade; a Spanish hall with an arched front arcade and a two-bell gable over its door; and a white Colonial house with green shutters, dormers and chimneys at both ends.
The battery is a low concrete block behind a grassy north slope rising to a parapet, with two round gun pits with iron rings, magazine doors and a stair on the south side, kept within y5; no roof dry-runs were done yet, since there's no build file, and no block named "chain" is used. Eight Presidio modules (white-wood houses, Mission duplex, garage, shed, brick barracks with colonnade, Spanish Colonial hall with belfry, officers' house, Endicott battery) on the architect's grid.
elements.md and plan.md (palette, 22 vocab helpers, rooms, parts) are written.
Six parts follow the trades: shells, roofs, chimneys, openings and trim, battery, lighting and grounds.

Masonry shells: parts/shells.mjs builds walls, plinths, bands, quoins, corner boards, floors and holes for stairs for plots 0-6, with the openings left as air. The hall has its nave, aisles, arcade piers and a stepped facade parapet. Plot 7 is left to the battery part. make.sh runs clean with no refused writes.
polish: Plot 7 (battery) not touched: that is the battery part's work.
Belfry, rose window, coping slabs and arch-head stairs on the hall are left to the fittings part.
Garage gable cells (20..21,4,4) float until the roof is laid under them; a few gable and parapet cells show as orphans until the roofs and fittings are in.
I only glanced at the render tiles and did not review them closely. I did not run `mcd fit` or `mcd walk`.

waste.cost: about 60 cells(...) calls
waste.tool: A helper that builds a hollow wall from the plan's OPENINGS table (face, position, size), so the opening cells are not typed twice.

waste.cost: 3 retries
waste.tool: Re-export B from vocab.mjs, or have make.sh fail loudly when a module does not load.

Finish the hall's belfry, arch heads and coping.

summary:
Roofs: parts/roofs.mjs lays the main roofs of plots 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 (reroof, palette-legal mixes, zero overhang) plus the Mission parapet, two door hoods, the shed's pyramid cap and two plot 6 dormers; plot 0 comes from roof.json (cottage, barn-red mix).
make.sh gives a whole build.nbt: Roofs 558 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette; fit OK; the street render reads as a red-tile, slate and dark-roofed post.
Not built: the overhangs (the roof tool shifts the build +1 in z when an eave reaches z=0), plot 4 gallery roof, plot 5 aisle lean-tos, arcade, belfry cap, plot 6 porch deck, and the 1-block-apron of the chimney keeps is untested.
polish: Overhangs: every reroof spec uses overhang 0 (plots 1, 2, 4, 5, 6) because overhang 1 makes reroof shift the roof +1 in z and overwrite the duplex's north wall at y5 (roof tool bug or footplate-at-z1 gotcha). Restore overhang 1 once the shift is fixed in the roof tool or the footprint is moved off the grid edge. plan.md wants overhang 1 for all of them.

roof.json (plot 0) overhang 1 reaches z0 and leaves 14 ORPHAN smooth_quartz stairs/slab on the eave at z0 and x0 (mcd check); the eave probably suffers the same shift, so check it with the overhang fix.
Plot 4 gallery roof (deepslate_tile_slab y6 x30..41 z11..12) not built.

Plot 5 aisle lean-tos (granite_stairs x44..46 and x61..63, z3..14), arcade shed (granite_slab at z17 and granite_stairs at z18, x49..58, y4), and belfry cap (smooth_sandstone_slab y10 x52..55 z16) not built.
Plot 6 porch deck (deepslate_tile_slab y3 x66..73 z8..9 and deepslate_tile_stairs facing north at z10) not built.
Plot 1 curved parapet and hoods are placed but not checked by eye at the duplex front; the front-elevation render was not inspected.
Plot 2 gable verge and the white gable wall at z4 not checked by eye. No trusses (roof.json has no trusses key) and no plan.md checklist ticks yet.

waste.what: Found by trial which palette blocks the roof tool's named palettes (red-tile, slate, dark-slate, barn-red) reach for: mud_brick, tuff_brick, polished_blackstone_brick, mangrove, spruce slab, and that the default soffit is spruce. Each fix was a dry run and a make.sh.
waste.cost: about 4 make.sh runs and 6 node probes, roughly 10 minutes
waste.tool: A roof palette check that takes the kit's palette.json and maps each named roof palette onto palette blocks (or reports the off-palette ones before writing), and a roof.json soffit default taken from the palette.

waste.what: Chased the duplex wall loss by hand: wrote single-file probes to see which reroof call overwrote wall cells at y5, then read the roof tool's shift output. The shift is the same +1 z drift the memory warns about, triggered by an overhang reaching z=0.
waste.cost: about 5 probe calls; the fix was to drop overhang to 0 on plots 1, 2, 4, 5, 6
waste.tool: reroof should report a shift (and refuse or warn) when an overhang reaches the grid edge, and accept footprint-relative placement so plot-level overhangs never touch z0.

waste.what: Refused writes and orphan roof edges were read from the make.sh report and mcd check, then localised by printing one cell at a time.
waste.cost: about 6 g.get calls
waste.tool: parts-report.json with the refusing cell's earlier owner (which part and which helper), and mcd check listing the orphan's neighbour cells.

waste.what: Hand-built the pieces that vocab helpers already cover (mission parapet, hoods, pyramid cap, dormers) only after checking their signatures in vocab/h1-h3.mjs, which was a read-then-call loop.
waste.cost: 2 file reads
waste.tool: A short signature index (vocab's helper list with arguments) in the kit so a worker does not read vocab sources.

companions.task: Lay the plot 4 gallery roof (the deepslate tile slab course at y6 over x30..41 z11..12) and the plot 6 porch deck, and check the slate courses against the stepped eave.
Build the plot 5 aisle lean-tos and the arcade shed (granite stairs and slabs at the head and the arch cells) so each stair course has its own facing without my checking each one.
Set the belfry cap (smooth_sandstone_slab over x52..55 z16 at y10) and the parapet course above the hall's facade, and confirm the cap sits flush on the parapet.

summary:
Chimneys: parts/chimneys.mjs builds the five exterior stacks (plots 0, 4 west/east, 6 west/east) via chimney(): five lit campfires over hay, flues, a deepslate_bricks band and brick_slab corner caps.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt; the Chimneys line shows 6 refused writes (5 are shell/roof cells, 1 is the roof slab at [5,7,3]) and no off-palette blocks.
Fit is clean on plots 4 and 6; plot 0 still reports one chimney fire, cured only by a roof keep box at x5 z2..4 y6..8 (tested, then reverted since roof.json is not mine).</summary>
<parameter name="waste">[{"what":"Worked out each stack's fire cell, footprint and flue column by hand from the architect's table, and found the chimney() `into` convention (the room side, not the fire side) by reading the library source, because the table says 'into: east' for a fire that lies east.","cost":"about 6 coordinate sets plus one source read and one failed guess","tool":"Use chimney_for(g, plot) from vocab/h3.mjs (it already holds the table) or document `into` as the room side in plan.md's chimney table."},{"what":"Added the band and cap by hand because chimney() lays neither, and then found by trial that a slab beside the flue reads as roof and fails fit, so I moved the cap to the corners.","cost":"three make.sh + fit cycles","tool":"chimney() options band: material and cap: 'slab' that keep the flue's face neighbours as full masonry, so fit passes first time."},{"what":"Tested the plot 0 fix (a roof keep box at the flue's house-side wall) by editing roof.json, rebuilding, then restoring the file.","cost":"two extra make.sh runs and a backup/restore","tool":"A chimney-aware roof step (roof keep boxes derived from the chimney table) or a chimney-first fit report naming the roof cell to keep."}]
polish: Plot 0 chimney fire fault: the roof's dark_oak_slab at [5,7,3] walls the flue. Needs roof.json keep box {from:[5,6,2],to:[5,8,4]} (tested: fit clean). roof.json is the roofs worker's file; I restored it unchanged.
Lintels over the five hearth mouths are refused: the shell wrote white_concrete or bricks at the mouth's y2 cell. Mouths are open at y1 only, with no lintel stair.
Cap is brick_slab on the top corners only: a slab beside the flue reads as roof, so the four face-adjacent ring cells stay full brick. Not a full step-out cap, since plot 0 has no room to step out.
Plot 0 has a second fit item at [5,8,3] (bricks on a bottom slab) that disappears with the roof keep box; no action in this part.

companions.task: Cut the cottage roof back from the plot 0 flue's house-side wall (x5 z2..4 y6..8), so the eave slab at [5,7,3] stops against the stack.
Leave the mouth's lintel course open at y2 in the shell (the wall cells at [5,2,3], [30,2,7], [41,2,7], [66,2,4], [73,2,4]), so the upside-down stair lintel can be laid over each hearth.

summary: Openings and trim: parts/fittings.mjs fills every OPENINGS cell of plots 0-6: glass_pane windows, the doors (single and double, with the hall's arch heads), shutters flat on the wall, duplex door hoods and Mission parapet, the house porch rails, the barracks colonnade, the hall rose window and belfry with two bells.
polish: Plot 5 main door: the terracotta surround (x52/x55 y1..3, x53..54 y4) is a shell wall cell, not air, so it is not written; the door stands on plain smooth_sandstone. Needs a shell-side change or a replace pass.
Plot 0 porch roof (brick_slab y3) and plot 6 porch deck (deepslate slab y3) are roofs-part work; the porch posts, rails and floors are done.
Dormer windows x67 and x72 at z6 y7 float (reported by mcd check) until the roofs part builds the dormer walls at z5..6 y7.
Plot 2 garage: the door pair and side door are placed; the white gable z4 y4 that the check reports floating belongs to the shells/roofs parts, not fittings.
Plot 0 chimney hearth mouth (x5 z3 y1) and the plot 6 hearth mouths are chimney part cells, not written here.
Clockmaker's clock face: plan.md has no clock on the hall or elsewhere, so none was built; the belfry carries the bells only.

waste.cost: about 10 rails and posts, plus one retry after the first pass left the connections wrong
waste.tool: a vocab fence helper (like window()) that sets north/south/east/west from neighbours, with a multi-cell run form

waste.cost: 9 stair cells, plus a refusal-driven rewrite
waste.tool: arch(g, ..., { jambs: false }) or an arch variant that writes only the stair row

waste.cost: one full make.sh run plus a retry
waste.tool: plan.md's FLOORS / shells notes should say which floors shells lays, so fittings does not repeat them

waste.cost: 4 cells by hand
waste.tool: window(g, cell, face, { block: 'orange_stained_glass_pane' }) or a pane() helper with a block parameter

waste.what: Checked the look by eye with four zoom renders and the front elevation tile; the front elevation at this scale is too small to read the openings.
waste.cost: 4 zoom renders and 3 reads
waste.tool: mcd zoom with a per-opening check, or a fit-style check that lists unglazed windows and shutters in the wrong cells

waste.what: zsh does not word-split an unquoted $MCD variable, so the command failed until I used the full path inline.
waste.cost: one failed Bash call
waste.tool: a shell wrapper script named mcd on PATH, or a note in the kit to call node $MCD explicitly

companions.task: Set the window and pane connections on the duplex bay and the hall rose window, and check the panes that float until the dormer walls land.
Lay the hall's arch heads and the terracotta surround as one job, so the surround can replace the shell's wall cells in one pass rather than leaving the door on plain stucco.
Check the two bells in the belfry hang from the beam as the attachment ceiling expects, and that the louvres let them show from below.

summary:
Coastal battery: Plot 7 coastal battery built in parts/battery.mjs: weathered concrete emplacement and parapet, deck, two gun pits with iron rings and pivots, banquette, two magazines with iron door pairs and rust, deck stair, iron-bar rail, glacis and side mounds.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt; the battery line shows 1176 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette, and fit reports OK. Zoom renders from north and south read as the battery.
Ticked the seven Plot 7 items in elements.md and added a battery Notes section to plan.md.
polish: Magazine rooms (x78..83 and x86..91, y1..2, z18..20) and the deck have no light from this part: the lighting and grounds part must hang lanterns in each room and by the battery's deck and glacis.
The iron-bar rail connection states are set by hand (east/west true), so the stub ends at the stair gap point into air; accepted for now, not verified in a close-up render.

waste.cost: about 25 fill/set calls and one mound loop, plus a few minutes of arithmetic on the mound heights and the deck-stair cells
waste.tool: a battery plan helper that takes the plan's Battery detail as data (box per course, pit centres, magazine boxes) and emits the fills, or a block-set helper that accepts plain and minecraft: ids and the state object for iron_bars, so the connection states are not hand-set

waste.what: Checked the iron-bar rail connections and the banquette slabs by eye in the zoom renders, not with a tool.
waste.cost: two zoom renders, one read each
waste.tool: a fit or check rule that reports iron_bars and fence connections that point into air

companions.task: Lay the weathered concrete courses (andesite foot, light grey body) and the parapet, and set the stone banquette slabs, so the mix is hand-picked rather than hashed.
Hang lanterns inside both magazine rooms and on the deck and glacis, so no mob spawns there; this is the part 6 gap noted in plan.md.
Check the deck stair's landing and headroom at the top step against the rear wall and the rail gap, since it is the only walked route up onto the deck.

summary:
Lighting and grounds: parts/grounds.mjs places 63 lanterns and lamp posts: hanging lanterns in every room and under porches and hoods, lamp posts at the garage apron, hall door, nave centre line and side walls, battery deck corners and glacis. make.sh saves a whole build.nbt with no refused writes and no off-palette blocks.
Light: all measured rooms are 8+ except one hall cell at 7 (measured with a temp rooms file in /tmp; the run's rooms.json is empty).
Not built: apron paths (palette has no path block) and the cypress trees (P6 "Presidio feel" item).
polish: Hanging lanterns depend on ceilings from other parts: house 0 bedroom (y6 roof), porch lanterns (brick_slab y3), duplex upper units (y6 roof), duplex door hoods (y3 granite stairs), garage (y3 plate/roof), officers' porch (deck slab y3). In this copy those cells are air, so `$MCD check` reports them unsupported; they should be supported once the roofs and openings parts land. Re-run check after the merge.
Battery lamp posts at the deck corners (y4) and the glacis posts (y2) float in this copy because the battery's deck and glacis are not built here (battery part is a stub). Re-check after the merge.
Apron paths not built: palette.json has no path block (dirt_path, gravel, cobblestone) and the ground course is smooth stone only. Needs a palette addition to do the door-to-gate path.
Cypress trees (elements.md P6 'Presidio feel' item) not built; no cypress placement is in this part's coordinates yet.

rooms.json is empty, so `$MCD room`/`light` with the run's rooms file map nothing; I measured with /tmp/grounds-light/rooms.json. Plan.md has no tick list in my copy, so I ticked the lighting item in elements.md only; plan.md's Notes unchanged.

waste.what: Worked out each lantern and lamp-post coordinate by hand from the plan's ROOMS and OPENINGS text, room by room.
waste.cost: about 60 coordinates computed by hand, plus two retries after reading the light maps
waste.tool: a `lantern_spots` helper or `mcd room --place` that picks hanging spots under the real ceiling and clears the dark cells, fed from rooms.json boxes.

waste.what: rooms.json is empty, so `mcd light` and `mcd room` mapped no rooms until I wrote a temp rooms file with 17 boxes from plan.md ROOMS.
waste.cost: one hand-written rooms file and several light runs
waste.tool: fill rooms.json from plan.md ROOMS at kit setup (or `mcd light --box` for ad hoc boxes).

waste.what: Checked the outdoor lamp posts by eye on the street render, which draws the whole 94-block street too small to read a post.
waste.cost: one render and a read of a 560 px tile
waste.tool: `mcd zoom` at each lamp post (battery deck, glacis, garage apron) with `--radius 3`.

waste.what: No path block in palette.json, so the apron paths the trade calls for cannot be written.
waste.cost: not built
waste.tool: add dirt_path / cobblestone / gravel to the palette's ground role, plus a `path()` helper in the vocabulary.

companions.task: Check the hanging lanterns against the finished roofs, porches and hoods once they merge, and fix any lantern whose ceiling is air.
Lay the door-to-gate apron paths (2 wide, slab steps) and the cypress trees, once the palette has a path block.
Confirm the deck and glacis the lamp posts stand on are built, and set the post and lantern cells on the deck walk.

summary:
inspection: Both checks now pass: WALK ok (rooms: none listed, reachedCells 97) and FIT reports OK. The 5 chimney fires were fixed by carving the roof where each chimney's house-side wall runs (roof.json, roofs.mjs).
The 18 floating lanterns and the bottom slab are fixed by a porch slab at x2/x4 and by ceiling blocks above each lantern (grounds.mjs). ./make.sh produces build.nbt.
Two plan items were missing from the build and are now stood in for: the plot 0 porch roof (two slabs, not the full row, because a full slab row blocked the walk) and the hall aisle lean-tos (granite blocks over four lanterns).
polish: WALK reachedCells is 97, down from 99 in the brief. Ok is still true and rooms is empty, so no room is affected, but I did not confirm which two cells were lost; the two porch slabs at [2,3,6] and [4,3,6] are the likely cause.

Hall aisle lean-tos (plan: granite_stairs at x44/x45/x46, y2..4) are not built. Four single granite blocks at y4 over the aisle lanterns (46,4,6), (46,4,11), (61,4,6), (61,4,11) stand in for them and are not the plan's roof.

Plot 6 porch deck (plan: deepslate_tile_slab y3 over x66..73 z8..9, stairs at z10) is not built. Only the two slabs at (67,3,9) and (72,3,9) were added to light the porch lanterns; the rest of the porch roof is still missing.
Plot 0 porch roof (plan: brick_slab y3 over x1..5 z6..7) is not built. Only two slabs at (2,3,6) and (4,3,6) were added, because a full row over the entrance column x3 blocked the walk.
The FIT list in the brief showed 8 of the 18 floating lanterns. The other 10 were found by re-running the check; I fixed all of them.

waste.what: I found the 18 floating lanterns only by re-running FIT after each fix. The brief listed 8 and said '18 floating' without naming the other 10.
waste.cost: 2 extra make.sh and check cycles, one of them a rebuild to test the porch slab
waste.tool: fit should print every issue (or the full list in --json) instead of truncating after 8 of 18 lines

waste.what: I did not know which blocks the walk treats as blocking headroom. I learned by trial that a bottom slab over the entrance column cuts the porch-to-house route (walk fell from 99 to 11), so I had to pick the slab cells by hand.
waste.cost: 1 rebuild plus walk, with a temporary edit and restore
waste.tool: walk should say which cell or headroom rule cut the route, e.g. 'blocked at [3,1,6]: slab at [3,3,6] lowers headroom'

waste.what: The plan's by-hand roofs (plot 0 porch, plot 5 aisle lean-tos, plot 6 porch deck) were never built, so their lanterns float. I had to work out each missing piece by searching the parts for what was there.
waste.cost: several greps across parts/ and a manual comparison with plan.md
waste.tool: make.sh (or runParts) could list plan.md by-hand elements that no part wrote, so missing hand roofs show up on the first build

waste.what: The chimney keep boxes: I worked out by hand which roof cell walls each flue (the house-side wall cell at y6..8) for all five stacks, one at a time.
waste.cost: about 5 coordinate derivations and 4 edits
waste.tool: fit's chimney-fire line could name the keep cell to add, e.g. 'add keep {from:[5,6,3],to:[5,8,3]} to roof spec'

build the plot 0 porch shed roof (brick slab y3, x1..5 z6..7) and the plot 6 porch deck (deepslate slab y3 x66..73 z8..9, stairs at z10), leaving the entrance column open
